successors.name: Muhammad Ali dynasty
successors.text: Diriyah and nearby cities 'ceded to the Ottomans', and the Hejaz, which the Egyptians held until 1840 (History of Saudi Arabia)

successors.name: Emirate of Nejd
successors.text: Najd, where the Al Saud returned in 1824 as the Second Saudi State

ledger.x: 1744: Muhammad bin Saud, emir of Diriyah, and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab sign the pact that founds the emirate.
1747: Muhammad bin Saud begins attacks on Riyadh.
1773: Riyadh falls to Abdulaziz after about 25 years of war.
1773: the long contest for Riyadh ends in Diriyah's favour (same sentence).
1789: Saud leads the emirate's forces into Al-Hasa.
1794: Qatif falls.
1794: the shape first reaches Asir (south to 16.4 N).
1795: Hasa is captured from the Bani Khalid.
1795: the contest for Al-Hasa ends with the capture.
1799: the shape adds central Asir and the northern Tihama.
1802: Taif and Khurma fall to the emirate.
1802: Bahrain comes under the emirate.
1803: Mecca is taken.
1803: the shape adds Najran, the whole of Asir, and the Yemeni Tihama as far as Hodeida.
1803: the shape adds Najran and the rest of Asir.
April 1804: Medina is captured.
1805: Saud takes part of Oman and the Buraimi Oasis.
1811: the Egyptian campaign opens in the Hejaz.
1811: Yanbu falls to Tusun Pasha's landing without a fight.
Late 1812: Medina falls to the Ottoman-Egyptian army after the Saudi defeat at Al-Safra.
1813: Jeddah is retaken without a fight 'about a month after Medina' (late 1812 or early 1813; the page's link is titled 'Battle of Jeddah (1813)').
January 1813: Mecca falls.
Early 1814: the Ottomans break the siege of Taif, and the town leaves the emirate; they held Al Qunfudhah 'only for about a month'.
Spring 1815: the Saudis are beaten and sign a treaty.
1815: the first round ends with the defeat and the unconfirmed peace treaty; Ibrahim Pasha resumes the war in 1816.
1816: Ibrahim Pasha resumes the war, 'with the assistance of French military instructors', and marches into the Najd; he launches the Najd campaign in September 1817.
1817: Al-Qassim falls.
1818 (bridging): Saudi suzerainty over Bahrain can have lasted no longer than the emirate.
9 September 1818: the siege ends.
9 September 1818: Abdullah bin Saud surrenders Diriyah to Ibrahim Pasha.

wars.name: Diriyah-Riyadh wars (Dahham ibn Dawwas)
wars.outcome: Riyadh captured by Abdulaziz in 1773 after nearly 25 years of battles and joined to the emirate.

wars.name: Saudi conquest of Al-Hasa from the Bani Khalid
wars.outcome: Qatif taken 1794 and Hasa 1795 (Abdulaziz page); Bani Khalid dominance eliminated 1792 and Al Hasa conquered 1789 (Saud page).

wars.name: Saudi conquest of the Hejaz
wars.outcome: Taif, Mecca and Medina pass to the emirate; Saudi control of the two holy cities 'by 1805' (Wahhabi War page).

wars.name: Wahhabi sack of Karbala
wars.outcome: A raid on the Shia holy city in Ottoman Iraq, reportedly killing up to 5,000; no territory held.

wars.name: Ottoman-Saudi War
wars.outcome: Ottoman-Egyptian victory under Tusun Pasha and then Ibrahim Pasha; Diriyah surrenders on 9 September 1818 and is razed.

wars.name: Siege of Diriyah
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Ibrahim Pasha arrived on 22 April 1818 and Abdullah surrendered on 9 September.

certainty.note: Oasis and tribal frontiers of central Arabia, the Hejaz coast and the Asir and Tihama highlands are approximate; no treaty or survey line defines any border of the emirate (the spring 1815 treaty was never confirmed).
